Most of what lies beneath the waters is deep under layers of mud and silt, moldering wood criss-crossing over algae covered stone and 
bone. Seams of minerals and deposits of gems lay unobtainable without incredible feats of effort, but an enterprising Traveler still has 
reason to find value in what these waters can produce, especially the ever bountiful fish. Where the waters sit still and thick, choked 
with algae and unmoving for seasons, the bluish-green-liquid vigael can be found, smelling of vinegar and fresh grass, it rises to the top 
in thin oily layers. Nestled between river stones are creekot oysters, filtering the quick moving waters and providing a very rich meat. 
In the Fenlands, while a pickax and shovel may not be of much use, a Traveler willing to get their feet wet may still find their fortune.
